title: Certificates of Deposit: The Standing a Certificate Needs to Take an In-Term Add-On
content:
An in-term add-on to a PCB certificate (Certificates of Deposit) is possible only where the certificate itself is of the right kind and in the right standing, whatever sum is in view. This page states those requirements.

## Requirements

An in-term add-on can be made to a certificate only if all three are true:

1. **Status.** The certificate's status on the bank's record is Active. An in-term add-on belongs to a running term, and only an Active certificate is in one.
2. **Opening deposit posted.** The certificate's ledger shows its opening deposit. A certificate that is still waiting for its opening deposit takes no add-on.
3. **Tier permits it.** The certificate's tier allows at least one in-term add-on in a term. On a tier whose in-term add-on count is zero, the question of size never arises.

If any one of them is false, no in-term add-on is accepted and nothing is written, whatever sum the owner has in mind.

## What each status means for an in-term add-on

| Status on the certificate record | In-term add-on possible? |
|---|---|
| Applied (awaiting the opening deposit) | No |
| Active | Yes, if the tier permits one and the opening deposit has posted |
| Grace period | No; the certificate is not standing in a running term |
| Closed | No |

The status is read from the record as it stands when the add-on is made. A certificate whose record still shows the grace period status stands outside any running term, however many days have passed since its maturity date.

## Point of judgement

**An owner of a 12-Month Certificate in Active status asks to add money mid-term (hypothetical).** If the tier's in-term add-on count is zero, nothing is accepted, even though the status requirement is met.
